candidates.hypothesis: Fast/medium EWMA trend (EWM-tau-4tau, tau 5-50 days) restricted to large-tick contracts (top half by volatility-normalised tick size) keeps its pre-2009 Sharpe; the post-2009 trend decay is confined to small-tick contracts (equity indices, FX).
candidates.mechanism: Self-fulfilling impact loop of CTA flow survives in dense (large-tick) order books; HFT liquidity withdrawal broke it in sparse (small-tick) books (Kurth et al. 2026).
candidates.best_source: Kurth, Eisler, Rej, Bouchaud (2026), Is Trend Still Your Friend? A Microstructural Account of the Demise of Short-Term Trend-Following, arXiv 2607.01550v1
candidates.sample: about 100 liquid futures, daily settlement, 1995-2025; break at 2008/9
candidates.post_2015_or_oos: post-break 2009-2025 is after the regime change; not a pre-registered OOS test
candidates.published_effect: large-tick tier Sharpe 1.0-1.2 post-break (about 1.4 pre-break); small-tick tier about 0; cost treatment not stated in passages read
candidates.dispersion: bootstrap standard errors shown in Fig. 11 (image, not read); all-contract Table 1 SE about 0.24-0.27
candidates.quote: Post-break, ST Sharpes collapse to essentially zero (mildly negative for the fastest signals), while LT Sharpes remain in the range 1.0–1.2.
candidates.decay_evidence: all-contract fast trend: tau=5 Sharpe 0.84 (1995-2009) -> 0.12 (2009-2025); HOP 1-month 0.06 in 2010-2016
candidates.data_needed: daily settlement/close and tick size for rates, grain, livestock roots
candidates.why: Only post-2009 trend evidence with Sharpe above 1 in a definable subset; directly bears on E22-F1 weighting. Multi-day, so not a Topstep candidate.
candidates.prop_notes: Not Topstep-compatible (multi-day). No evidence a day-session-only version keeps the premium (LPS 2019: equity-index TSMOM earns overnight). Multi-day track only (personal IBKR; firm allowing overnight holds).
candidates.overlap_note: Same EWMA-crossover family as E22-F1 (Carver EWMAC); differs by restricting to large-tick contracts and weighting fast speeds there. Conflicts with V39 'no further trend variant on 2010-2024'; the lead decides.

candidates.hypothesis: Cross-market overnight TSMOM: the US equity market's last half-hour return predicts the next day's first half-hour return of international equity markets.
candidates.mechanism: Late-informed trading / information spillover from the US close to foreign opens (authors' framing; full text not read).
instruments: CME-listed Nikkei futures (eligibility on Topstep unverified)
candidates.entry_window_ct: foreign open, e.g. Tokyo 09:00 JST = 19:00 CT (US daylight time) / 18:00 CT (standard time)
candidates.best_source: Xu, Li, Singh, Chen, Li (2025), Cross-market overnight time-series momentum, Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money 105, 102239
candidates.post_2015_or_oos: abstract: significant 'both in- and out-of-sample' (not verified)
candidates.published_effect: sign and significance only; no size in abstract
candidates.quote: We propose a new cross-market overnight momentum: the US stock market’s last half-hour return predicts the next day’s first half-hour stock returns in international markets.
candidates.data_needed: 1-min bars of CME Nikkei futures; US index futures last half-hour (owned: NQ, RTY, MES)
candidates.data_cost: not looked up (no Databento spend or quote in this stage)
candidates.why: Forward citation of MOP that yields a one-trade-a-day, 30-minute, in-window hold; unsized, so pointer-level only.
candidates.prop_notes: Inside Topstep 17:00-15:10 CT day; single trade, not HFT, no scheduled-news exposure; Nikkei availability on Topstep unverified.
candidates.overlap_note: K8 cross-market family and E.20 RTY E7 (Li-Sakkas-Urquhart, first->last half-hour) differ in direction and timing; R13 owns cross-market lead-lag.
